story: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission recommends data center moratorium Ordinance 2026-42 to the Assembly, 11-0, with five amendments (November 10th)

justified_repeats.reason: First call returned HTTP 503 (transient). One retry, also 503. Item reported unreachable.
First call returned HTTP 403. One retry in case it was transient, also 403. All S2 claims killed.

repeat_reasons.reason: HTTP 503 transient failure, one retry, still 503
HTTP 403 on first call, one retry, still 403

source_fetch_summary.notes: The other 17 distinct URLs were each fetched once: fileId=13403, KTUU S1, agenda 13383, events API, KUAC, HB0217B.pdf (403), fastdemocracy, akleg BASIS HB 217 (403, tried once as a second source for the bill history), gvea.com, notices 225521, 224684 and 224673, whitehouse pledge, simpler.grants.gov, govinfo HR 9340 RH, senate vote menu, FERC docketsheet. fileId=13403 (plainText) was NOT confirmed as the same staff report. The first 100,000 of its 774,898 characters are the agenda, the October 13th minutes and the RZ2027-003 staff report, with no Ordinance 2026-42 material. I did not page further. Every staff report and ordinance claim therefore cites the packet fileId=13440, verified against the local extraction of packet pages 1218 to 1225. P1 (the memo) was read from the five rendered images and not WebFetched, as instructed. P2 was read only from the local extraction.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission voted 11-0 to recommend that the Borough Assembly adopt Ordinance 2026-42 with amendments.
claims.verbatim: -Recommended (11-0) adoption to the Borough Assembly with the following amendments:
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: Read from memo-4.png, page 4, under ORDINANCE NO. 2026-42. The memo lists six amendment bullets, but the Line 33 water quality bullet is printed twice, at the bottom of page 4 and again at the top of page 5. That leaves five distinct amendments (C03 to C07). The memo never prints the word five, so the showrunner should declare that count. The memo header reads 'Regular Meeting Convened at 6:00 p.m./Adjourned at 12:35 p.m.', which most likely means a.m. No claim is built on the adjournment time.

claims.claim: Ordinance 2026-42 establishes a temporary moratorium on land use permits for large scale data centers and was sponsored by Mayor Hopkins.
claims.verbatim: An Ordinance Establishing A Temporary Moratorium On Land Use Permits For Large Scale Data Centers. (Sponsor: Mayor Hopkins) (Staff Contact: Kellen Spillman)
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-4.png. The same wording appears as item G.4 of the agenda, fileId=13383 (fetched).

claims.claim: The commission amended line 60 of the ordinance to add the word gross before floor area.
claims.verbatim: Line 60, add "gross" before "floor area"
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-4.png. The memo prints curly quotes, rendered here as straight quotes. Staff recommended this amendment, but the staff report says 'Amend line 59'. In the referred ordinance, 'floor area' sits on line 60, so the memo's line number matches the ordinance.

claims.claim: The commission amended line 60 to replace 50,000 with 40,000 in the floor area trigger.
claims.verbatim: Line 60, to strike "50,000" and replace with "40,000"
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-4.png. Staff recommended this one as well (C37). The unit is square feet of floor area, per the ordinance text (C20).

claims.claim: The commission amended line 33 to insert the words and impacting water quality after generating noise.
claims.verbatim: Line 33, to insert "and impacting water quality" after "generating noise"
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: Printed on memo-4.png and again on memo-5.png (page break duplicate). Line 33 is in the WHEREAS clause on adverse impacts (C31). This is a commission amendment, not one of staff's two.

claims.claim: The commission amended line 65 to move the moratorium end date from December 31st, 2027 to June 30th, 2028.
claims.verbatim: Line 65, to strike "December 31, 2027" and replace with "June 30, 2028"
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-5.png. Line 65 is Section 3, Moratorium Period (C24). Do not turn this into a number of months. The moratorium runs to a fixed date from an effective date that is not yet known.

claims.claim: The commission amended line 73 to change the study deadline from six months to ten months.
claims.verbatim: Line 73, to strike "six" and replace with "ten"
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-5.png. Line 73 is in Section 4: 'within six months of the effective date of this ordinance' (C26). KTUU corroborates: 'recommendations from six months to 10'.

claims.claim: Eleven Planning Commission members are listed as present at the November 10th meeting, and none were absent.
claims.verbatim: Members Absent and Excused None
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-1.png. The memo prints no total. 11 is a count of the printed names under 'Members Present': Walker Ringstad, Christopher Stepovich, Brittany Smart, Olivia Lunsford (Vice-Chair), Gregory Corbett, Kerynn Fisher, Joseph Collier, Kevin McKinley (Chair), Olivia Rodriguez, Eric Muehling, Jennifer Campbell. That matches the 11-0 votes. Ex officio members (Mayor Grier Hopkins, Community Planning Director Kellen Spillman) are listed separately.

claims.claim: Kevin McKinley is listed as chair of the Planning Commission.
claims.verbatim: Kevin McKinley, Chair
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-1.png, Members Present. Olivia Lunsford is listed as Vice-Chair.

claims.claim: The action memorandum covers the Planning Commission meeting of November 10th.
claims.verbatim: ACTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING OF NOVEMBER 10, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-1.png SUBJECT line. The agenda (fileId=13383, fetched) also gives November 10th at 6:00 p.m.

claims.claim: The action memorandum is dated November 13th and addressed to Mayor Grier Hopkins.
claims.verbatim: DATE: November 13, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-1.png. 'TO: Grier Hopkins, Mayor, Fairbanks North Star Borough'. From Aurora Marhenke, Assistant Clerk I, through April Trickey, MMC, Borough Clerk.

claims.claim: The same night, the commission voted 11-0 to sponsor and recommend adoption of the 2026 FNSB Regional Comprehensive Plan.
claims.verbatim: -Voted (11-0) to sponsor and recommend adoption to the Borough Assembly, adopting the 2026 FNSB Regional Comprehensive Plan with the following amendments:
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-2.png, under ORDINANCE NO. 2026-TBD, 'An Ordinance Adopting A Major Update Of The Fairbanks North Star Borough Regional Comprehensive Plan'. Agenda item G.3 (fileId=13383).

claims.claim: The commission attached 19 numbered amendments to its comprehensive plan recommendation, each adopted without objection.
claims.verbatim: 19. Amended (without objection) Chapter 5, Page 57, to modify Figure 28: Map of Interior Rivers so that it includes a Borough boundary line, a North arrow and a scale bar.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-2 to memo-4. Items 1 to 19 each begin 'Amended (without objection)'. Most are scrivener or wording edits. No comp plan amendment names data centers, so don't imply one does.

claims.claim: The memorandum says the next Planning Commission meeting is scheduled for December 15th.
claims.verbatim: The next meeting is scheduled for December 15, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, Department of the Assembly (action memorandum)
claims.notes: memo-5.png. Corroborated by the CivicClerk events API (C15).

claims.claim: The borough's meeting calendar lists a Planning Commission meeting on December 15th with no agenda published yet.
claims.verbatim: "eventName":"Planning Commission Meeting" "startDateTime":"2026-12-15T18:00:00Z" "publishedFiles":[]
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (CivicClerk meeting calendar)
claims.notes: JSON fields as relayed by the fetch tool. The 18:00Z stamp looks like local time with a Z suffix, since the commission meets at 6:00 p.m., so don't state a clock time from it. agendaId 5288.

claims.claim: The borough's meeting calendar lists a Regular Assembly Meeting on December 17th, and its agenda had not been posted when checked.
claims.verbatim: "eventName":"Regular Assembly Meeting" "startDateTime":"2026-12-17T18:00:00Z" "publishedAgendaTimeStamp":"" "publishedFiles":[]
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (CivicClerk meeting calendar)
claims.notes: With no agenda posted, nothing shows Ordinance 2026-42 will be on the December 17th agenda. Suggested phrasing: 'The Assembly next meets December 17th; its agenda isn't posted yet.' KTUU reports a likely vote on January 14th (C40). No January events were on this page of results (more pages exist).

claims.claim: The November 10th Planning Commission meeting was set for 6 p.m. in the Mona Lisa Drexler Assembly Chambers at the Juanita Helms Administration Center.
claims.verbatim: November 10, 2026, at 6:00 p.m., in the Mona Lisa Drexler Assembly Chambers, Juanita Helms Administration Center, 907 Terminal Street, Fairbanks
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda)
claims.notes: The fetch tool returned this passage reformatted, so the verbatim string may differ slightly in layout from the agenda. The memo independently prints 'Regular Meeting Convened at 6:00 p.m.' The agenda shows G.3 as the comp plan ordinance and G.4 as Ordinance 2026-42, and G.4 is the only data center item.

claims.claim: As referred, the ordinance defines a large-scale data center to include a facility with an aggregate peak electrical demand of five megawatts or greater.
claims.verbatim: has an aggregate peak electrical demand of five megawatts (5 MW) or greater
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1224, Section 2, lines 59 to 60. Verified against the local extraction pc_packet_p1218_1225.txt. The 135 MB packet was not WebFetched. The staff report (page 1219) repeats the definition.

claims.claim: As referred, the ordinance's second trigger is a facility occupying more than 50,000 square feet of floor area devoted to data center operations.
claims.verbatim: occupies more than 50,000 square feet of floor area 60 devoted to data center operations
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet pages 1224 to 1225. The '60' inside the verbatim is the printed line number. The commission recommends 40,000 square feet of gross floor area instead (C03, C04). Present this as the referred text.

claims.claim: The ordinance's third trigger is onsite electrical generation facilities with a generating capacity of five megawatts or greater.
claims.verbatim: includes onsite electrical generation facilities with a generating capacity of five megawatts (5 MW) or greater.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1225. The three triggers are joined by 'or', so meeting any one of them qualifies.

claims.claim: The ordinance states that under present zoning large-scale data centers would be permitted only in the GU-1 and GU-5 General Use Districts.
claims.verbatim: Under the present zoning ordinance, large-scale data centers would be permitted only in the GU-1 and GU-5 General Use Districts
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1224, lines 36 to 37. The next WHEREAS says the General Use Districts allow 'the widest range of land uses of any zoning district designation in the Borough'. The staff report separately says data center is not listed as a permitted or conditional use in any zone (C38). Those are two framings in the borough's own documents.

claims.claim: Section 2 says no land use permit applications for a large-scale data center shall be accepted, nor pending applications approved, while the moratorium is in effect.
claims.verbatim: no land use permit applications for a large-scale data center shall be accepted, nor pending applications approved, while this moratorium is in effect.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1224, lines 54 to 56. It opens 'Notwithstanding any provision of FNSBC Title 18 to the contrary'.

claims.claim: As referred, Section 3 keeps the moratorium in effect through December 31st, 2027 unless the Assembly ends or extends it sooner by ordinance.
claims.verbatim: The prohibition imposed by Section 2 of this ordinance shall be in effect through December 31, 2027, unless terminated sooner or extended by ordinance of the Assembly.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1225. The commission recommends June 30th, 2028 (C06). The staff report calls the referred term 'approximately one year (end of 2027)'.

claims.claim: Section 4 directs the Department of Community Planning to study data center impacts on energy usage, air quality, water usage and water quality, and noise pollution.
claims.verbatim: including but not limited to impacts on energy usage, air quality, water usage and water quality, and noise pollution.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1225. The full clause is 'shall study the impacts of large-scale data centers on the public health, safety, and welfare'.

claims.claim: As referred, Section 4 required the department's report and recommendations within six months of the ordinance taking effect.
claims.verbatim: within six months of the effective date of this ordinance.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1225. The commission recommends ten (C07). The report goes to the Planning Commission.

claims.claim: Section 5 makes the ordinance effective at 5 p.m. on the first Borough business day after its adoption.
claims.verbatim: This ordinance is effective at 5:00 p.m. on the first Borough business day following its adoption.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1225. The moratorium isn't in effect yet. It needs Assembly adoption.

claims.claim: The ordinance's first WHEREAS clause cites growing demand from artificial intelligence creating a need for physical infrastructure.
claims.verbatim: prior to growing demand from artificial intelligence creating a need for physical infrastructure
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1223, lines 14 to 15. This is the AI hook in the borough's own words.

claims.claim: The ordinance says the borough's Regional Comprehensive Plan was last updated in 2005.
claims.verbatim: Comprehensive Plan (Comprehensive Plan or Plan) was last updated in 2005
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1223, lines 13 to 14. The staff report agrees: 'the existing Comprehensive Plan was adopted in 2005'.

claims.claim: The ordinance says the Comprehensive Plan update is expected to be finalized in early 2027.
claims.verbatim: the Comprehensive Plan update is still in progress and expected to be finalized in early 2027
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1223, lines 25 to 26. This is a projection, so write it as 'expected to be finalized in early 2027'.

claims.claim: The ordinance warns large data centers could consume a significant share of available electrical power, generate noise and degrade air quality.
claims.value: significant share of available electrical power
claims.verbatim: including consuming a significant share of available electrical power, generating noise from cooling and power equipment, and degrading air quality through emissions from onsite power generation facilities
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet pages 1223 to 1224, lines 31 to 34. The clause is framed as a possibility ('could have substantial adverse impacts'), so keep 'could'. Water quality is added here by the commission amendment (C05).

claims.claim: The ordinance header prints its referral to the Planning Commission as 10/22/2026.
claims.verbatim: Referred to the Planning Commission: 10/22/2026
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission (agenda packet, Ordinance 2026-42 as referred)
claims.notes: Packet page 1223, header lines 2 to 3 (line numbers removed from the verbatim). This conflicts with the staff report's October 26th (C32). Report both, attributed, and don't pick one.

claims.claim: The staff report says the Assembly referred Ordinance 2026-42 to the Planning Commission on October 26th.
claims.verbatim: Ordinance No. 2026-42 was referred by the FNSB Assembly for Planning Commission recommendation on October 26, 2026 (Attachment A).
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report, in Planning Commission agenda packet)
claims.notes: Packet page 1218. Conflicts with C31. The staff report is cited at fileId=13440 because fileId=13403 couldn't be confirmed as the same document (see source_fetch_summary).

claims.claim: Staff wrote that the state's marijuana licensing timeline took about 18 months from the 2014 vote to the first license, which acted as a de facto moratorium.
claims.verbatim: The state did institute a timeline through their licensing process that took about 18 months from the vote to when the first license was approved. This licensing process essentially acted as a de facto moratorium
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report, in Planning Commission agenda packet)
claims.notes: Packet page 1220. This is a staff characterization of history ('The FNSB went through a very similar process in 2014 and 2015'). Attribute it to staff.

claims.claim: Title 18 defines a large scale development to include a retail or wholesale building exceeding 55,000 square feet of gross floor area.
claims.verbatim: exceed(s) 55,000 square feet of gross floor area
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report, in Planning Commission agenda packet)
claims.notes: Packet page 1219, quoting FNSBC 18.04.010. The staff report is the fetched document. The code itself wasn't fetched.

claims.claim: Title 18 also defines a large scale development as an entertainment facility exceeding 40,000 square feet with seating for 800 people or more.
claims.verbatim: An entertainment facility exceeding 40,000 square feet and which has a seating capacity of 800 people or more.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report, in Planning Commission agenda packet)
claims.notes: Packet page 1219. This explains the 40,000 square foot amendment, since staff wanted to 'align large-scale data centers with other somewhat like uses in code'.

claims.claim: Staff recommended two amendments, adding gross before floor area and changing 50,000 square feet to 40,000 square feet.
claims.verbatim: Community Planning recommends the following two amendments to provide uniform oversight.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report, in Planning Commission agenda packet)
claims.notes: Packet page 1221, followed by 'Amend line 59 to add gross before floor area' and 'Amend line 60 to change 50,000 square feet to 40,000 square feet.' The other three adopted amendments (C05, C06, C07) came from the commission itself.

claims.claim: The staff report says the borough zoning code has no definition for data center and does not list it as a permitted or conditional use in any zone.
claims.verbatim: There is currently no definition for data center in the FNSB zoning code. It is not listed as a permitted or conditional use in any zone
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report, in Planning Commission agenda packet)
claims.notes: Packet page 1219. See the note on C21 for how this sits beside the GU-1 and GU-5 clause.

claims.claim: The staff report says the Community Planning Department has received inquiries about data centers potentially being developed in the community.
claims.verbatim: There have been inquiries received by the FNSB Community Planning Department on data centers potentially being developed in the community.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report, in Planning Commission agenda packet)
claims.notes: Packet page 1221. No number of inquiries and no developer names are given, so don't add either.

claims.claim: The staff report says the Municipality of Anchorage has researched and passed data center regulations.
claims.verbatim: There are many municipalities in the United States and even Alaska that have researched and passed regulations regarding data centers, including the Municipality of Anchorage.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Department of Community Planning (staff report, in Planning Commission agenda packet)
claims.notes: Packet page 1220. Attribute it to FNSB staff ('according to borough planning staff'). I didn't verify an Anchorage ordinance independently.

claims.claim: KTUU reported, citing Mayor Hopkins, that an Assembly vote will likely take place on January 14th.
claims.verbatim: a vote will likely take place on Jan. 14
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF), Alex Bengel
claims.notes: Published 'Nov. 16, 2026 at 3:34 PM AKST' even though the URL path says 11/17. This is a projection, single-sourced and attributed. No posted agenda corroborates it (the December 17th agenda isn't up and no January event appeared). Suggested phrasing: 'a vote is likely January 14th, the mayor told KTUU'.

claims.claim: Mayor Hopkins told KTUU that adoption is when the clock will start for the 18-month moratorium.
claims.verbatim: That's when the clock will start for the 18-month moratorium
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF), Alex Bengel
claims.notes: The verbatim quote appears on the page. 18-month is the mayor's round figure. The amended ordinance actually runs to a fixed date, June 30th, 2028, so the real length depends on the adoption date. Present it as his quote and don't restate it as fact.

claims.claim: KTUU reported the commission's changes as extending the mayor's proposed 12-month timeframe to 18.
claims.verbatim: extending the mayor's proposed 12-month timeframe to 18
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF), Alex Bengel
claims.notes: This is KTUU's framing, not a primary figure. The ordinance prints end dates, not month counts. Use it only as 'according to KTUU', or rely on the primary date change (C06).

claims.claim: Mayor Hopkins told KTUU a data center that comes in purely for a government purpose would, he believes, not be subject to the moratorium.
claims.verbatim: If it comes in as purely for a government purpose, I believe that would be not subject to our moratorium and our regulations
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF), Alex Bengel
claims.notes: The verbatim quote appears on the page. It's an opinion ('I believe'), so keep the hedge. Context is the Eielson Air Force Base passage (C44).

claims.claim: KTUU reported Hopkins is confident any proposed data centers outside the Eielson Air Force Base fence would be under borough jurisdiction.
claims.verbatim: While confident any proposed data centers outside of the Eielson Air Force Base fence would be under borough jurisdiction
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF), Alex Bengel
claims.notes: This is the reporter's paraphrase of the mayor, not a direct quote. Attribute it 'as reported by KTUU'. The Air Force background about Eielson land offers couldn't be verified this run because af.mil returned 403 twice (see killed).

claims.claim: Hopkins told KTUU the scale of what happens in other cities before they can act is relatively terrifying.
claims.verbatim: The sheer scale of what you see happening in other cities that pop up before they can take action is relatively terrifying
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF), Alex Bengel
claims.notes: The verbatim quote appears on the page, attributed to Hopkins by KTUU.

claims.claim: KTUU reported the Borough Assembly voted unanimously to send the ordinance to the Planning Commission.
claims.verbatim: the borough assembly voted unanimously to send the ordinance to the Planning Commission
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU/KTVF), Alex Bengel
claims.notes: Single-sourced. No vote tally was checked against Assembly minutes. Attribute it 'according to KTUU'.

claims.claim: Waymo is testing its self-driving taxis in Fairbanks, KUAC reported on November 16th.
claims.verbatim: But can it swing through a coffee hut? Waymo is testing its self-driving taxis in Fairbanks
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (KUAC), Shelby Herbert
claims.notes: Headline. Published November 16th, 3:04 PM AKST. The article gives no vehicle count, and a caption says a resident 'spotted a couple Waymo test vehicles' near the airport.

claims.claim: A Waymo spokesman told KUAC by email that the tests will be performed with a specialist at the wheel.
claims.verbatim: the tests will be performed with a specialist at the wheel
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (KUAC), Shelby Herbert
claims.notes: The spokesman declined an interview, and this email line is the only company comment.

claims.claim: KUAC reported that Governor Mike Dunleavy announced the Waymo testing in a post on X.
claims.verbatim: Gov. Mike Dunleavy announced the testing in an X post
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (KUAC), Shelby Herbert
claims.notes: The fetch tool relayed this as a summary, so the verbatim may be paraphrased. Re-confirm the wording before quoting. The X post itself wasn't fetched. The article doesn't mention HB 217 or any Alaska AV law.

claims.claim: HB 217, which regulates autonomous vehicles, passed the Alaska House on April 30th with 39 yeas and one excused.
claims.verbatim: (H) PASSED Y39 E1
claims.source_outlet: FastDemocracy (mirror of Alaska Legislature BASIS bill history)
claims.notes: The official sources, akleg.gov PDF HB0217B and BASIS, both returned 403, so this rests on a mirror reproducing BASIS action lines. E1 means one excused, not a no vote. Attribute it 'according to the legislative record'. The mirror lists the latest text as HB0217E (AM SCS CSHB 217(TRA)), not the B version the scout cited.

claims.claim: On May 17th the Senate State Affairs Committee reported HB 217 with two do not pass and one do pass recommendations.
claims.verbatim: (S) STA RPT SCS(TRA) 2DNP 1DP
claims.source_outlet: FastDemocracy (mirror of Alaska Legislature BASIS bill history)
claims.notes: DNP were Bjorkman and Tilton, DP was Gray-Jackson. Mirror only, since the official site returned 403.

claims.claim: HB 217 was referred to the Senate Rules Committee on May 17th, its last recorded action.
claims.verbatim: (S) Referred to RULES
claims.source_outlet: FastDemocracy (mirror of Alaska Legislature BASIS bill history)
claims.notes: The mirror shows no later action. It doesn't say the bill died. See killed.

stories_surviving: Fairbanks Planning Commission recommends Ordinance 2026-42 data center moratorium 11-0 with five amendments
Waymo testing in Fairbanks, and HB 217 stalled in Senate Rules (runner-up, mostly secondary sourcing)

killed.claim: The Department of the Air Force has offered land at Eielson Air Force Base among sites for AI data center leases (S2).
killed.why: af.mil article 4456660 returned HTTP 403 on both attempts. With no fetched source this run, no Air Force claim can be used. KTUU (C44) mentions Eielson only as jurisdiction context.

killed.why: No fetched page says this. KTUU only quotes Hopkins wanting 'to talk to [Golden Valley Electric Association] about what their grid situation looks like'. The gvea.com homepage has no data center item.
No fetched page says the bill died. The mirror shows only 'Referred to RULES' as the last action. Use 'stalled in Senate Rules' or 'its last action was a referral to Senate Rules'.

killed.why: Not printed in any primary source. The ordinance uses a fixed end date and an effective date that depends on adoption. The showrunner declares any arithmetic separately. KTUU's '18-month' appears only as an attributed quote or framing (C41, C42).

killed.why: The memo prints 'Adjourned at 12:35 p.m.', which is likely a typo for a.m. Per the brief, no claim is built on it.

killed.why: The memo prints no count, and one bullet is duplicated across the page break. Five distinct amendments is a derived count (see C01 notes).

killed.claim: KTUU reported the commission vote as 11-0 and reported the water quality amendment.
killed.why: Neither appears in the KTUU article. Both rest on the primary memo (C01, C05).

killed.claim: fileId=13403 is the same staff report as the packet pages.
